text.title: Readiness Checklist — Worked Examples
text.summary: A rendered readiness.md, the public-surface inventory used by item 9, and the concrete evidence examples for the conditional items and the surface-coupling grep.

example.code:
# readiness: F012-billing-export
- [x] 1. ACs evidence — tests/api/test_export.py::test_csv_columns; screenshots/F012-export-success.png - [x] 2. Tasks done — tasks/todo/ and tasks/in-progress/ empty - [x] 3. Commit hygiene — `feat(F012-T01): add CSV export endpoint` … no trailers, no emoji - [x] 4. CI green — https://ci.example.com/runs/4471 - [x] 5. API tests — backend touched (apps/billing/views.py); pytest apps/billing/tests/api/ passed in run 4471 - [ ] 6. Playwright pos+neg — n/a: no user-facing flow (export triggered by an existing button) - [ ] 7. UI heuristics — n/a: no UI impact, no rendered element changed - [x] 8. Spec delta — project-spec/api.md#billing-export drafted in this PR - [x] 9. Surface coupling — grep `path: /billing` project-spec/api.md → sibling /billing/invoices; no overlap - [ ] 10. Deployed — pending: nero-prod per project-spec/deploy.md
verdict: blocked (item 10)
example.note: Items 6 and 7 are not-applicable with a reason naming what the feature does not touch, so they do not block. Item 10 is empty, so the feature stays in in-progress/.
Feature touches `apps/billing/views.py` → API tests required → reviewer confirms `pytest apps/billing/tests/api/` passed in CI artefact.

section.title: What counts as a public surface (item 9)

list.item: Skill description / triggers (the auto-router keys off these).
API path or method signature exposed to clients.
CLI flag, subcommand, or environment variable consumed externally.
Public type/class/function name exported from a library boundary.
Database table or column name read by downstream systems.

section.title: The surface-coupling grep (item 9)

example.note: Adding skill `sdd-batch-orchestrator` → grep `description:` across `skills/faion/workflows/` → find sibling `sdd-promotion-gate-checklist`. Verify keyword overlap is minimal; if not, narrow one description.

section.p: The empirical anchor: F001 in the faion plugin defined a skill trigger description. F002 later added an unrelated trigger description. The two descriptions overlapped at the keyword layer, so the auto-router fired the wrong skill for several user inputs. The bug was invisible at code-review because each PR only looked at its own diff. The fix was retrofitting an explicit surface-coupling review — item 9 is the result of that one specific historical failure.

list.item: Items 5, 6, 7 are conditional on what the feature actually touches; pinning the conditions is what stops the reviewer from waiving them by claiming inapplicability without justification.
readiness.md is the last artefact in done/ — the audit trail is the evidence links, not the ticks.
